{{See also|Probabilistic number theory}}

In mathematics, the '''Kubilius model''' relies on a clarification and extension of a finite probability space on which the behaviour of [[additive arithmetic function]]s can be modeled by a sum of [[independence (probability theory)|independent]] [[random variable]]s.<ref>{{cite conference
 | last = Schwarz | first = W.
 | editor1-last = Grigelionis | editor1-first = B.
 | editor2-last = Kubilius | editor2-first = J.
 | editor3-last = Pragarauskas | editor3-first = H.
 | editor4-last = Statulevičius | editor4-first = V.
 | contribution = Some aspects of the development of probabilistic number theory
 | location = Vilnius
 | mr = 1649606
 | pages = 661–701
 | publisher = TEV
 | title = Probability theory and mathematical statistics: Proceedings of the 6th International Conference held in Vilnius, June 28–July 3, 1993
 | year = 1994}}; see [https://books.google.com/books?id=9UMOvAsTXVkC&pg=PA674 p. 674]</ref>

The method was introduced in [[Jonas Kubilius]]'s monograph ''Tikimybiniai metodai skaičių teorijoje'' (published in Lithuanian in 1959)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://old.mii.lt/?siteaction=pages.browse&page=istorija_skerus|title=MATEMATIKA LIETUVOS MOKSLŲ AKADEMIJOJE|accessdate=14 April 2018}}</ref> / ''Probabilistic Methods in the Theory of Numbers'' (published in English in 1964) .<ref>J.Kubilius {{Google books|2TEJAQAAQBAJ|Probabilistic methods in the Theory of Numbers}}</ref>

Eugenijus Manstavičius and Fritz Schweiger wrote about Kubilius's work in 1992, "the most impressive work has been done on the statistical theory of arithmetic functions which almost created a new research area called Probabilistic Number Theory. A monograph (''Probabilistic Methods in the Theory of Numbers'') devoted to this topic was translated into English in 1964 and became very influential."<ref>{{cite book |editor1-first=Eugenijus |editor1-last=Manstavičius |editor2-first=Fritz |editor2-last=Schweiger |title=Analytic and probabilistic methods in number theory |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PewI8EsBTWEC |accessdate=2009-04-17 |series=New Trends in Probability and Statistics |volume=2 |year=1992 |publisher=VSP |location=Utrecht |isbn=978-90-6764-094-7 }}</ref>{{Rp|xi}}
